mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in FOMC policy
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 5.25%; or IC > 0.05 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 6.5% coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor-market participation reduces risk aversion and boosts equity demand.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with rising unemployment
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive such triggers, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05); or IC < -0.1 in walk-forward evaluation.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 2% for two consecutive months, it predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as excess demand supports equity pricing.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 2% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong consumption growth
failure_condition: Over 100 such instances, 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline (IC > 0.05); or the interaction coefficient is insignificant in OLS.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO by at least 8% followed by a rise in HOUST by more than 10% predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as contractionary supply shocks depress market valuations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by ≥8% AND HOUST > previous month by >10%
regime_hint: Supply shock episode (e.g., oil price spike)
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, 5-day forward returns are not negative (IC > 0.1); or the interaction is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent monthly declines in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% for three consecutive months are associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as lower inflation expectations reduce real discount rates.
failure_condition: Across 50 such windows, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (IC < 0.05); or the effect is only present in in-sample period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in PAYEMS (labor market activity) by at least 15% in a month predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as increased hiring signals economic resilience and equity optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above previous month by ≥15%
failure_condition: Over 40 such triggers, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (IC > 0.1); or the effect reverses in out-of-sample.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 10% in a month relative to the prior month, it predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand erodes earnings expectations.
failure_condition: Over 30 such events, 20-day forward returns are not negative (IC > 0.05); or the effect is absent in periods of stable retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side easing cycle (indicated by a sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of ≥4% for two months) is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate future capacity expansion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by ≥4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During 10 such transitions, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (IC < 0.1); or the effect is only present during non-crisis periods.
